title: A coherent module killed by the maximal ideal at the generic point of an integral closed subscheme contains a pushforward of ideal sheaves, isomorphically near that point
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], i.e. locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z$ an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], let $\eta$ be the generic point of $Z$ (the unique point whose closure is $Z$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]) and $\xi=i(\eta)$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] whose stalk $\mathcal F_\xi$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is annihilated by the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_\xi$ of the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Then there are an integer $r\ge0$, a coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$, an injective $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\alpha:i_*(\mathcal I^{\oplus r})\to\mathcal F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], where $\mathcal I^{\oplus r}$ is the direct sum of $r$ copies of $\mathcal I$ and $i_*$ the pushforward of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], and an open neighbourhood $W$ of $\xi$ in $X$ such that the restriction $\alpha|_W$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YE (label lemma-prepare-filter-irreducible, coherent.tex line 2982); its proof uses Properties 01PO (properties-lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), Lemmas 01Y3 (lemma-local-isomorphism), 087T (lemma-i-star-equivalence), 01Y4 (lemma-map-stalks-local-map), 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open) and Schemes 01J3 (reduced induced structure)

proof.text: (Preliminaries on $Z$ and the ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$.) $i$ is an immersion, hence locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](2), so $Z$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]; $i$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $i(Z)$ of the quasi-compact space $X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and a closed subset of a quasi-compact space is quasi-compact, so $Z$ is quasi-compact, i.e. $Z$ is a Noetherian scheme. On $X$ and on $Z$, $\mathcal O$ is coherent and coherent means quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; kernels, cokernels and finite direct sums of maps of coherent modules, and quasi-coherent submodules of coherent modules, are coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](1),(2); in particular $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}$ is coherent, and the restriction of a coherent module to an open subscheme is coherent (the conditions of [pqf-def-coherent] concern only the opens of that subscheme). Let $\mathcal J=\ker(i^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ be the ideal sheaf of $i$; it is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], hence coherent and so of finite type. Claim: $\mathcal J_\xi=\mathfrak m_\xi$. The ring map $\rho:\mathcal O_{X,\xi}\to\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$, $a_\xi\mapsto(i^\sharp a)_\eta$, is the composite of the stalk map $i^\sharp_\xi:\mathcal O_{X,\xi}\to(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_\xi$ and the bijection $c_\eta:(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_\xi\to\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](2). $i^\sharp$ is surjective as a map of sheaves [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $i^\sharp_\xi$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks], and $\ker(i^\sharp_\xi)=\mathcal J_\xi$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](2). Hence $\rho$ is a surjective ring map with kernel $\mathcal J_\xi$ onto $\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$, which is a field because $Z$ is integral with generic point $\eta$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk]. So $\mathcal J_\xi$ is a maximal ideal of the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$, i.e. $\mathcal J_\xi=\mathfrak m_\xi$ [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YE (lemma-prepare-filter-irreducible, coherent.tex line 2982), proof, first paragraph ('J_xi = m_xi'); the Noetherianity of Z and the computation of J_xi are written out here

proof.text: (Replacing $\mathcal F$ by the sections killed by $\mathcal J$.) Let $\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F$ be the subsheaf of sections annihilated by $\mathcal J$ [lem-weil-pbc-sections-annihilated-by-ideal] ($\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent of finite type and $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent, step 1). By (1) of that lemma $\mathcal F'$ is a quasi-coherent submodule of the coherent $\mathcal F$, hence coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](2). By (3), $\mathcal F'_\xi=\{s\in\mathcal F_\xi:\mathcal J_\xi s=0\}=\{s\in\mathcal F_\xi:\mathfrak m_\xi s=0\}=\mathcal F_\xi$ (step 1 and the hypothesis on $\mathcal F_\xi$). So the stalk at $\xi$ of the inclusion $\iota:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$, which is injective [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](1), is bijective, and by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-local-isomorphism](4) there is an open neighbourhood $W_1$ of $\xi$ in $X$ with $\iota|_{W_1}$ an isomorphism. Moreover $\mathcal J\mathcal F'=0$ (the image of $\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F'$): for every $x\in X$, $(\mathcal J\mathcal F')_x=\mathcal J_x\mathcal F'_x$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk](2), which is $0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sections-annihilated-by-ideal](3); a module whose stalks all vanish is $0$, since its map to $0$ is bijective on stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YE (lemma-prepare-filter-irreducible, coherent.tex line 2982), proof, first paragraph (Properties 01PO, Lemma 01Y3)

proof.text: (Descent to $Z$.) $X$ and $Z$ are locally Noetherian (step 1), $\mathcal F'$ is coherent and $\mathcal J\mathcal F'=0$ (step 2). By the essential surjectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence](1) (Stacks 087T) there are a coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$ and an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\theta:i_*\mathcal G\to\mathcal F'$. In particular $\mathcal G_\eta\cong(i_*\mathcal G)_\xi\cong\mathcal F'_\xi$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](2).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YE (lemma-prepare-filter-irreducible, coherent.tex line 2982), proof, second paragraph (Lemma 087T)

proof.text: (A map $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal G$ near $\eta$.) Let $K=\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$, a field (step 1). As $\mathcal G$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], there are an open $U_0\ni\eta$ and a surjection of sheaves $\mathcal O_{U_0}^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal G|_{U_0}$; its stalk $K^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal G_\eta$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks] (the stalk of a finite direct sum is the direct sum of the stalks, filtered colimits commuting with finite sums [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]). So $\mathcal G_\eta$ is a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space; let $r=\dim_K\mathcal G_\eta\ge0$ and choose a $K$-linear isomorphism $\psi_0:(\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r})_\eta=K^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal G_\eta$. $Z$ is locally Noetherian and $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}$, $\mathcal G$ are coherent (step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-stalk-map-extends] (Stacks 01Y4) there are an open $U\ni\eta$ of $Z$ and an $\mathcal O_U$-linear $\varphi:\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}|_U\to\mathcal G|_U$ with $\varphi_\eta=\psi_0$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-local-isomorphism](4) on the locally Noetherian open subscheme $U$ to the coherent modules $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$, $\mathcal G|_U$ (step 1) gives an open $V$ with $\eta\in V\subseteq U$ and $\varphi|_V$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YE (lemma-prepare-filter-irreducible, coherent.tex line 2982), proof, third paragraph (r = dim F_xi finite; Lemmas 01Y4 and 01Y3)

proof.text: (Extending $\varphi$ over $Z$.) Let $T=Z\setminus U$, a closed subset of $Z$, and $\mathcal I_T\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of the reduced induced structure on $T$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](1) (Stacks 01J3): $\mathcal I_T(U')=\{f\in\mathcal O_Z(U'):f(t)=0\text{ in }\kappa(t)\ \forall t\in T\cap U'\}$. Then $\{z\in Z:(\mathcal I_T)_z\neq\mathcal O_{Z,z}\}=T$: for $z\in U$, $1\in\mathcal I_T(U)=\mathcal O_Z(U)$ (the condition is empty), so $(\mathcal I_T)_z=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$; for $z\in T$ every element of $(\mathcal I_T)_z$ is a germ $f_z$ with $f(z)=0$, i.e. $f_z\in\mathfrak m_z$ [def-weil-residue-field], so $(\mathcal I_T)_z\subseteq\mathfrak m_z$. Thus $U=Z\setminus V(\mathcal I_T)$ in the notation of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-homs-over-open] (Stacks 01YB). Apply that lemma on the Noetherian scheme $Z$ (step 1) to the quasi-coherent $\mathcal G$, the coherent $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}$, the ideal $\mathcal I_T$ and $\psi=\varphi$: there are $n\ge0$ and an $\mathcal O_Z$-linear $\chi:\mathcal I_T^n\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal G$ with $\chi|_U=\varphi$ under $(\mathcal I_T^n\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r})|_U=\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$. Put $\mathcal I=\mathcal I_T^n$ ($\mathcal I=\mathcal O_Z$ if $n=0$): a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections](1), coherent since $Z$ is locally Noetherian (step 1) [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](2). Moreover $\mathcal I\,\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}=\mathcal I^{\oplus r}$ as submodules of $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}$: the tensor product commutes with finite direct sums and $\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z}\mathcal O_Z\cong\mathcal I$ (both hold for the presheaf tensor product and pass to sheafifications [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), and under $\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}\cong\mathcal I^{\oplus r}$ the multiplication map is the componentwise inclusion $\mathcal I^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}$, whose image is $\mathcal I^{\oplus r}$. So $\chi:\mathcal I^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal G$, $\chi|_U=\varphi$; in particular $\chi|_V=\varphi|_V$ is an isomorphism and $\chi_\eta=\varphi_\eta$ is bijective.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YE (lemma-prepare-filter-irreducible, coherent.tex line 2982), proof, third paragraph (Schemes 01J3, Lemma 01YB, 'I^n(O_X^r) = (I^n)^r')

proof.text: ($\chi$ is injective; the 'easy proof omitted' of the source.) Let $\mathcal K=\operatorname{Ker}\chi\subseteq\mathcal I^{\oplus r}\subseteq\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}$ (sectionwise kernel). It is coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](1), and $\mathcal K_\eta=\ker(\chi_\eta)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](2) (step 5). For $j=1,\dots,r$ let $p_j:\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_Z$ be the inclusion into $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}$ followed by the $j$-th projection. Its image $\operatorname{Im}p_j$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](1),(2), with $(\operatorname{Im}p_j)_\eta=(p_j)_\eta(\mathcal K_\eta)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](4). As $Z$ is integral with generic point $\eta$, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk] ((a)$\Leftrightarrow$(c)) gives $\operatorname{Im}p_j=0$, so $p_j=0$ for every $j$. A section of $\mathcal K$ over an open $V'$ is a section of $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}(V')=\mathcal O_Z(V')^{\oplus r}$ all of whose coordinates $p_j(s)$ vanish, hence $\mathcal K=0$: $\chi$ is injective on the sections over every open of $Z$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YE (lemma-prepare-filter-irreducible, coherent.tex line 2982), proof, last sentence ('injective because X is integral and it is injective at the generic point (easy proof omitted)'), written out here

proof.text: (Pushing forward; conclusion.) Let $\alpha=\iota\circ\theta\circ i_*\chi:i_*(\mathcal I^{\oplus r})\to i_*\mathcal G\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$. It is $\mathcal O_X$-linear, $i_*$ being a functor from $\mathcal O_Z$-modules to $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-module-pullback]. On an open $W'\subseteq X$, $(i_*\chi)_{W'}=\chi_{i^{-1}W'}$, since $(i_*\mathcal H)(W')=\mathcal H(i^{-1}W')$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks]; so $i_*\chi$ is injective on every open (step 6), and $\alpha$, a composite with the isomorphism $\theta$ (step 3) and the inclusion $\iota$, is injective. The set $i(Z\setminus V)$ is closed in $X$, because $Z\setminus V$ is closed in $Z$ and $i$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $i(Z)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; let $W_2=X\setminus i(Z\setminus V)$, an open set containing $\xi=i(\eta)$ ($\eta\in V$, $i$ injective), with $i^{-1}(W_2)=V$. For every open $W'\subseteq W_2$, $(i_*\chi)_{W'}=\chi_{i^{-1}W'}$ with $i^{-1}W'\subseteq V$ is bijective (step 5), so $(i_*\chi)|_{W_2}$ is an isomorphism. Let $W=W_1\cap W_2$, an open neighbourhood of $\xi$ (step 2). Then $\alpha|_W=\iota|_W\circ\theta|_W\circ(i_*\chi)|_W$ is a composite of isomorphisms. With $r\ge0$ (step 4) and the coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ (step 5) this proves the lemma.
